issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
Add a SkyRL callback that detects long rollout drains, asks a local LLM judge which outstanding traces are probably stuck, and automatically terminates and masks every trace the judge recommends stopping. A drain waits for already-dispatched training rollouts after new dispatch pauses for validation or training shutdown. Judge and cancel individual rollout attempts; each retry has its own attempt ID and partial trace. The judge should favor early termination when uncertain, so one trace cannot hold the allocation for another full agent attempt.

In long-loop run `long-loop-full-2026.11.12.5` on 256 H100s, validation drains took 32m00s at step 2, 38m32s at step 4, and 56m24s at step 8. The final step-8 straggler first ran for 1,801.65 seconds, failed to upload verifier tests to a closed sandbox, then replayed the whole agent for another 1,800.35 seconds. The retry finally timed out and was graded 0. The first attempt began before the drain, so the two agent durations exceed the measured drain time. The retry-scope repair in #11120 addresses that replay; this feature should also handle other tails that cannot be identified by a fixed exception list.

The current wait is [`TrainingContext.pause_and_drain`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2baaaf40d6ca1eb8c3d8699b6d7c0e943b369ce7/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/context.py#L233), reached through [`RayPPOTrainer._evaluation_session`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2baaaf40d6ca1eb8c3d8699b6d7c0e943b369ce7/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/trainer.py#L1631). A step-end callback that runs only after this await returns cannot interrupt the drain.

Done when:

- A callback runs periodically inside validation and final-training drains after configurable elapsed-time or lack-of-progress thresholds. It receives the outstanding attempt IDs, phases, age, last model/tool/verifier progress, configured deadlines, retry history, and relevant partial traces.
- It automatically starts a local judge through existing Marin inference tooling, reusing a warm judge when available. Reuse the serving/model configuration used by [`local_inference`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2baaaf40d6ca1eb8c3d8699b6d7c0e943b369ce7/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/serve.py#L30) and the [existing hosted-judge pattern](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2baaaf40d6ca1eb8c3d8699b6d7c0e943b369ce7/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/runner.py#L662). Pin the judge model, runtime, prompt and sampling configuration. Judge startup and inference have bounded budgets and explicit resources within the run's allocation cap.
- The judge analyzes possibly stuck traces and returns a validated structured verdict: attempt IDs to terminate or keep waiting, reasons, and uncertainty. Its prompt explicitly favors terminating early when in doubt. Trace contents are treated as untrusted evidence, never as instructions to the judge.
- The framework consumes the verdict, cancels each selected attempt through its normal cleanup path, and marks it as an infrastructure exclusion with a distinct reason such as `drain_judge_early_stop`. Every selected trace is masked from policy loss, advantages and baseline statistics; it must not become a scored zero or trigger a whole-agent retry. Release its leases and settle pending group/drain bookkeeping so the drain can finish. Apply the configured minimum eligible group size after masking; reject groups that become too small through normal admission accounting. Record lost groups by route and do not dispatch replacement attempts during the drain.
- Cancellation is idempotent and bound to the exact attempt. Ignore stale recommendations for attempts that already finished. Unrelated trials, shared serving workers, checkpoints and snapshots remain untouched. Ordinary model-limit outcomes continue to be graded unless the judge explicitly selects them for early termination.
- Retain every judged trace, judge input/output, model and prompt pins, reason, timestamps and cancellation result. Keep the original observed condition alongside the infrastructure-mask disposition. Report per-source exclusion rates, judge cost and time, remaining configured attempt budget at cancellation, and cancellation-to-drain-completion time. Any estimated time saving must be labeled as an estimate. Early stopping can censor useful slow work; make that effect measurable rather than claiming the judge proved an infrastructure fault.
- CPU tests with fake rollout workers and a fake judge cover a stuck trace releasing the drain, masking with no zero reward or retry, normal completion racing a verdict, malformed or timed-out judge responses, and cleanup failure. Judge failures are reported and do not add an unbounded wait; fallback behavior is explicit in the run config.

This request is for the feature; it does not change the running long-loop experiment. Supporting measurements: `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/long-loop/evidence/20261112-rl5/drain-watchdog-request/observations.json` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Flong-loop%2Fevidence%2F20261112-rl5%2Fdrain-watchdog-request%2Fobservations.json)).

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

`TrainingContext.pause_and_drain()` stops dispatch and awaits all group tasks; it has no periodic hook or attempt-level view. The retry loop is inside a worker, and each Harbor attempt receives a new ID and trace after the coordinator has dispatched its group. Final training reaches this drain through final evaluation when enabled; otherwise shutdown cancels outstanding work. [PR #11120](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11120) is open and already repairs verifier-failure retry scope; no open PR implements this judge feature.

**Relevant code**
- [`context.py#L233`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2baaaf40d6ca1eb8c3d8699b6d7c0e943b369ce7/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/context.py#L233) — drain waits for group tasks
- [`trainer.py#L1631`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2baaaf40d6ca1eb8c3d8699b6d7c0e943b369ce7/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/trainer.py#L1631) — validation drain entry
- [`task_worker.py#L525`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2baaaf40d6ca1eb8c3d8699b6d7c0e943b369ce7/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/task_worker.py#L525) — worker retry loop
- [`agent_runtime.py#L203`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2baaaf40d6ca1eb8c3d8699b6d7c0e943b369ce7/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/agent_runtime.py#L203) — attempt ID and evidence path
- [`group_admission.py#L320`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2baaaf40d6ca1eb8c3d8699b6d7c0e943b369ce7/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/group_admission.py#L320) — minimum eligible group check

# Proposed Fix

Add an opt-in, pinned drain judge at the SkyRL worker/coordinator boundary. This needs an attempt registry, cancellable trial control, new exclusion accounting, and a bounded local inference service; it is larger than a safe single-pass fix. Implement against the SkyRL revision containing #11120's retry repair so the two changes do not compete over the retry loop. No change is proposed for the running `long-loop-full-2026.11.12.5` run.

1. **Expose attempt state.** Register each attempt at creation, including group/route, phase (`agent`, tool, verifier, cleanup, retry backoff), start and last model/tool/verifier progress, configured deadlines, retry index/history, and a reference to its partial trace. Use the existing fresh Harbor attempt ID as the cancellation key. Emit completion/removal atomically so a verdict can be checked against live state. Keep bounded, redacted trace excerpts for the judge and preserve full attempt evidence under the existing retention path.
2. **Run a bounded callback inside the drain.** Extend `pause_and_drain()` to evaluate elapsed-time and no-progress thresholds while waiting. Add an explicit final-training drain before finalization when outstanding training rollouts exist, with dispatch still paused and no replacement work. The callback receives a snapshot of live attempts; it does not cancel a group or Ray actor merely because one attempt is slow. Require finite attempt, judge-startup, judge-inference, and cleanup budgets in the opt-in config.
3. **Judge locally.** Reuse a warm pinned endpoint if available; otherwise start a local server through [`local_inference`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2baaaf40d6ca1eb8c3d8699b6d7c0e943b369ce7/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/serve.py#L29), following the existing [judge-session pattern](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2baaaf40d6ca1eb8c3d8699b6d7c0e943b369ce7/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/runner.py#L662). Pin model revision, serving runtime, prompt version, and sampling parameters; reserve its CPU/GPU and memory within the run's 256-H100 cap. Give the judge only delimited trace data and state that trace text is untrusted. Validate a structured verdict with exact live attempt IDs, `stop`/`wait`, reason, and uncertainty; the prompt favors stopping when uncertain. Reject unknown IDs, malformed output, and over-budget calls. Configure a finite fallback deadline and explicit action for judge failure.
4. **Cancel and settle.** Recheck the attempt ID under worker ownership, then cancel only that trial through its normal cleanup/finally path. A completed attempt makes the recommendation stale; duplicate recommendations have no effect. Record `drain_judge_early_stop` as an infrastructure exclusion before retry selection, retain the observed condition separately, and route the result through the existing [`loss_masks` and `exclude_from_baseline` projection](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2baaaf40d6ca1eb8c3d8699b6d7c0e943b369ce7/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/task_projections.py#L330). Settle the group lease and buffer disposition after cleanup, apply the configured minimum eligible group size, and count rejected groups by route. Do not synthesize a scored zero, restart the agent, or affect other trials, serving workers, checkpoints, or snapshots. Keep ordinary model-limit outcomes graded unless selected by the judge.
5. **Evidence and verification.** Retain each judged attempt's partial trace, judge request/verdict and pins, timestamps, original condition, exclusion and cancellation result. Report per-source exclusions, judge time/cost, remaining attempt deadline, lost groups, and cancellation-to-drain-completion time; label any saved-time calculation as estimated. CPU tests with fake workers and judge cover stuck release, masks and retry suppression, completion racing verdict, malformed/timeout responses, and cleanup failure. Run the affected SkyRL tests, required lint/types, and the repository's PR review gate before a PR.

The main tradeoff is censoring useful slow work. Reviewers should confirm where a warm local judge can live within the fixed allocation and choose the explicit failure fallback and hard drain budget before implementation; the exclusion and timing metrics will measure the effect after rollout.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
PR #10735's process-scope cleanup breaks a Terminal-Bench 2.1 verifier and leaves additional Daytona trials unscored. A matched 20-task RNO2A run used Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B at revision `37561816e66b5b9153b1b64c10968c18c1e6f4a0`, Terminus-2, one attempt per task, and a 900-second agent timeout. The baseline scored 19/20 tasks with 7 solves. The PR head scored 12/20 with 4 solves and failed its coverage gate. Independent model samples limit aggregate reward comparisons; the trial and error evidence below identifies the cleanup regression.

Reproduce:
1. Run Terminal-Bench 2.1 registry ref 6 on the fixed 20-task panel at baseline commit `2baaaf40d6`. The task list and resolved policy are in the [baseline archive](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fevals%2Fpr-10735-tb2%2Fpr10735-before-20261112-tb2-20-3e94c250d95f5bdb9fde39e563239fa5%2Fresults).
2. Run the same panel, model revision, serving shape (H100×4), and timeouts at PR head `be7450c233`. The [PR archive](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fevals%2Fpr-10735-tb2%2Fpr10735-after-20261112-tb2-20-8dba55fc7de851149c71e40517aa97ff%2Fresults) contains its task results.
3. Inspect `git-multibranch` and the unscored trial exceptions.

Both `git-multibranch` agents hit the 900-second timeout. The baseline verifier passed (reward 1). The PR trajectory shows SSH and nginx listening before timeout; its verifier then failed (reward 0) with `ssh: connect to host localhost port 22: Connection refused`. [SingleStepTrial._run_agent](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/be7450c233/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/trial/single_step.py#L69) catches `AgentTimeoutError` and proceeds to verification, but [Trial._run_agent_phase](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/be7450c233/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/trial/trial.py#L651) preserves services only when the agent phase has no exception. The PR therefore stops the service before a verifier that still runs. The PR's `qemu-alpine-ssh` attempt failed with `AgentProcessScopeStartError` before any agent turn.

Seven PR trials had new unscored process or command errors: five `Cannot collect Daytona command output`, one `AgentProcessScopeStartError`, and one `PhaseCancellationError` from unconfirmed cleanup. One verifier timeout was unscored in each arm. The baseline's three initial Daytona setup failures were retried in the same archive and produced task results. Raw result roots: `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/evals/pr-10735-tb2/pr10735-before-20261112-tb2-20-3e94c250d95f5bdb9fde39e563239fa5/results` and `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/evals/pr-10735-tb2/pr10735-after-20261112-tb2-20-8dba55fc7de851149c71e40517aa97ff/results`.

Expected: Verifier-dependent tasks retain agent-started services through verification when a tolerated agent timeout occurs. Final task teardown stops those services. Other tasks reach verification or report a confirmed cleanup failure without wedging Daytona command output.

Recommended work:
- Fix the lifetime decision for the pinned verifier-dependent tasks on tolerated agent timeouts. Explicit cancellation should still stop the sandbox. Test an agent that starts SSH, times out, remains reachable to the verifier, and is stopped at teardown.
- Investigate a backend-owned `Shellbox Machine.kill_processes()` contract before extending the guest subreaper. Reuse Local's cgroup containment and prove that Daytona and QEMU can stop detached descendants. This addresses the [duplicate Local cleanup](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10735#discussion_r4488269083), [host CPython upload](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10735#discussion_r4488269089), and [Machine API](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10735#discussion_r4520096922) review threads. Check whether the long-lived Daytona command transport contributes to the five output-collection timeouts.
- Rerun the pinned 20-task panel after the fix. Require `git-multibranch` verifier parity, no process-scope setup failures, and scored coverage comparable to the baseline before making PR #10735 ready.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

PR #10735 is draft and owns this regression. `Trial._run_agent_phase()` retains the two pinned Terminal-Bench services only when the agent exits normally, while `SingleStepTrial._run_agent()` records `AgentTimeoutError` and still runs the verifier. The current lifetime test asserts service cleanup on timeout; the seven newly unscored trials also involve process-scope startup, Daytona output collection, and cleanup confirmation.

**Relevant code**
- [`trial.py#L607-L682`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/be7450c233/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/trial/trial.py#L607-L682) — phase cleanup and task pins
- [`single_step.py#L69-L84`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/be7450c233/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/trial/single_step.py#L69-L84) — timeout remains scoreable
- [`test_trial_service_lifetime.py#L115-L185`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/be7450c233/vendor/harbor/tests/unit/test_trial_service_lifetime.py#L115-L185) — timeout expects cleanup
- [`machine.py#L194-L203`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/be7450c233/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/machine.py#L194-L203) — Machine lacks process teardown
- [`daytona/machine.py#L388-L424`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/be7450c233/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/daytona/machine.py#L388-L424) — output read timeout path

# Proposed Fix

1. Update the agent phase on #10735 so a tolerated timeout for the two digest-pinned tasks stops the active agent turn but retains services already started for verification. Keep explicit trial cancellation and failed cleanup terminal. Replace the timeout expectation with a real-process test: start an SSH-like service, time out the agent, reach it from the verifier, then confirm task teardown stops it. Test cancellation separately.
2. Move process ownership and confirmed teardown into Shellbox's Machine contract. Reuse Local's cgroup containment; prove Daytona and QEMU stop detached descendants without trusting guest-writable completion markers. Specify how agent commands are separated from task sidecars and services intentionally retained for a verifier. 2. When the driver-log read reaches Finelog's snapshot deadline, the collector exits 1 despite the succeeded ferry.

Expected: an optional driver-log read failure yields a partial report warning and preserves the successful canary result. The same collector failure affected the [tier-1 ferry](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11255) earlier today.

## Canary run context

- Lane: `datakit-tier2`; date: 2026-11-12 UTC
- Iris job: `/runner/iris-run-job-20261112-155057` (succeeded, exit 0, 0 failures, 0 preemptions)

- [W&B run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin/runs/datakit-tier2-ferry-43252103908-1)

OPD and Grug passed in the same [Actions run](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/43268375464).

Expected: `FetchLogs` serves the completed job's native log so the gate can check its metrics. The uploaded streaming artifact includes four training steps but not the complete metric record, so the gate result cannot be reconstructed from it.

issues.author: muchanem
issues.body:
`shellbox.Machine` has no operation that stops processes a command left behind. Each Docker exec runs under `sh -c` in its own `setsid` session, and the backend only interrupts the command's process group on timeout or cancellation, so a background loop started by an agent command outlives that command and keeps running on the machine.

This matters when a task grades on the agent machine. In #9769 the verifier writes `verdict.json` to a fresh `mktemp -d` directory and the engine reads it in the same exec, but a surviving agent process running as the same user can still scan for the new directory and rewrite the verdict while the verifier runs. `FileReward` has the same exposure at its fixed reward paths. The engine cannot sweep processes itself: on Docker the container's init and any daemons started by setup look the same as the agent's orphans from inside the container.

Reproduce:
1. Run a shell task whose agent executes `while :; do printf '{"status":"scored","reward":1}' > /logs/verifier/verdict.json; done &` and then finishes.
2. Grade with a verdict-file verifier on the agent machine.
3. The loop is still running after the agent command returns and can overwrite the verifier's output.

Expected: before grading, the engine can ask the machine to terminate every process started by agent commands, leaving the container init and processes started by setup or by the grader untouched.

Done when:
- `Machine` exposes an operation that terminates the processes started by a given set of commands (or by all agent commands since a marker), on the Docker, Iris and ShellSim backends.
- The rolloutengine verdict-file and file-reward graders call it before running a verifier on the agent machine.
- A test shows a background writer started by an agent command cannot replace the verdict.

Context: the Codex P1 thread on #9769, https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9769#discussion_r4201632563 (thread PRRT_kwDOLj5faM6ps_0m).

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

`_ShellboxTaskSession.advance()` runs agent `sh -c` commands on the task machine, and `_grade_rollout()` later runs collection and the verifier there when no separate verifier environment is configured; `Machine` has no way to identify or stop processes left by the agent. PR #9769's fresh verdict directory narrows the race, but a live agent process can discover it while grading. No open PR found in the duplicate-work check implements this cleanup; #9769 is still open, and #9844 changes Iris exec retry behavior in an overlapping file.

**Relevant code**

- [`machine.py#L138-L153`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e9859a4e80c57e8a6290220fafc6896a470c6e62/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/machine.py#L138-L153) — shared machine contract
- [`docker/machine.py#L52-L83`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e9859a4e80c57e8a6290220fafc6896a470c6e62/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/docker/machine.py#L52-L83) — exec lifetime
- [`iris/machine.py#L151-L189`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e9859a4e80c57e8a6290220fafc6896a470c6e62/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/iris/machine.py#L151-L189) — remote exec lifetime
- [`task_session.py#L143-L175`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7e2196900094fddcaf9c3ce2f9c7f49e3e4f72ad/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/task_session.py#L143-L175) — agent command and grade boundary
- [`grading.py#L95-L128`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7e2196900094fddcaf9c3ce2f9c7f49e3e4f72ad/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/grading.py#L95-L128) — same-machine verifier path

# Proposed Fix

## Design

Add an opaque, machine-owned process scope to Shellbox: `open_process_scope() -> ProcessScope`, `run(command, *, scope: ProcessScope | None = None) -> Result`, and `terminate_process_scope(scope) -> None`. Run only agent shell calls in the scope. Setup, health checks, artifact transfer, and verifier commands remain outside it. Termination must be idempotent, prevent new commands in that scope, wait until its live processes are gone, and raise if the backend cannot establish that result. Update every `Machine` implementation to satisfy the contract or report unsupported scope creation explicitly; Docker/gVisor, Iris, and ShellSim are required for this issue.

First test a worker-owned, per-scope process container (a cgroup v2 scope is one candidate) on Docker and Iris gVisor. It must retain detached descendants, including children that call `setsid` or double-fork, while preserving container init and setup daemons. A `killpg` or parent-PID scan does not meet that contract. If either backend cannot provide this containment, reject same-machine scoped grading there and use a separate verifier environment. For ShellSim, terminate retained simulated jobs; if its synchronous runner cannot retain any, prove that invariant with a behavior test and make termination explicit. The Docker/gVisor implementation can share the Docker path; QEMU and Daytona must either implement the scope or reject tasks that require it before agent execution.

Create one scope after task setup, attach it to each agent shell command, and terminate it before `verifier.collect`, private file installation, or verifier execution. For staged tasks, terminate the stage's scope before its grade and open a new scope for the next stage. A failed termination must prevent the verifier from running and surface as an infrastructure failure, never a reward. Keep a separate verifier machine for adversarial file and verdict grading: stopping processes cannot undo agent changes to setup daemons or private paths made before the stop.

## Costs and risks

The change crosses the Shellbox contract and every backend, and PR #9769's Rollout Engine code is still on a stacked branch. Backend containment is the feasibility gate; silently treating process-group termination as complete would leave the reported race open.

## Testing

Start with a failing Rollout Engine regression: an agent command leaves a bounded writer running, the verifier writes a lower reward, and the observed grade must be the verifier's result. Add backend behavior tests that detach a child, terminate the scope, and verify the child stops while a setup daemon survives; also cover repeated termination and failure before grading. Use the existing local Iris RPC fixture and ShellSim suite, with a Docker-marked test for the real container boundary and an Iris sandbox check in dedicated CI. Test FileReward, VerdictReward, and a stage boundary. Run `uv run pytest lib/shellbox/tests/ lib/rolloutengine/tests/`, `./infra/pre-commit.py --all-files --fix`, and the pre-PR review when implementing.

## Open questions

- Which worker-side containment primitive is available for scoped execs on Iris gVisor and Docker? Confirm this with a detached-child proof before selecting the implementation.
- Should same-machine file/verdict grading be accepted for untrusted root agents after cleanup? I recommend requiring a separate verifier environment for that threat model, even when scope termination succeeds.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 The reported verdict overwrite path is no longer present on `main`. [#9937](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9937) requires separate Harbor verifier mode, and RolloutEngine's `grade_in_sandbox` creates a fresh machine for verdict-file and `FileReward` grading. [#9769](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9769) closed without merging. Agent processes can still race output capture and `ScriptGrader.collect` on the task machine, so stable collection remains an open problem.

I checked the current Docker boundary: a command cannot create a nested PID namespace (`unshare -Urpf` returns `EPERM`) or a cgroup (`/sys/fs/cgroup` is mounted read-only). Killing the recorded process group would stop the reported background loop, but a child that calls `setsid` survives. Iris currently exposes exec through its worker RPC, without a worker-owned process scope or snapshot operation. A `Machine` method backed by process-group signals would not meet this issue's “every process” contract.

I have not opened a PR for that incomplete cleanup. I recommend narrowing this issue to stable artifact collection and defining a worker-owned freeze/snapshot boundary for Docker and Iris, with a test that covers a detached child and confirms setup daemons survive. The existing fresh verifier machine already protects the verdict and reward paths.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 Research: #10735 puts a `ProcessScope` helper in Shellbox, but Harbor still prepares the guest supervisor, tracks scope commands, and confirms cancellation. `Machine` has no process-scope contract. Local already has cgroup-backed command quiescence. Daytona's current command stop uses a process group, and QEMU serializes foreground commands over its guest console. A Docker probe on this host found `/sys/fs/cgroup` mounted read-only inside an Ubuntu container. These paths need backend containment proofs before a shared API can promise confirmed teardown. The 20-task TB2 comparison in #11256 also found a timeout-path service regression and seven new unscored failures.

Proposed fix: add an opaque, machine-owned scope whose termination blocks new scoped commands, waits for detached descendants, and reports failure when completion cannot be established. Keep setup, sidecars, relays, and verifier commands outside it. Prove the contract for the backends #10735 uses, including Daytona and QEMU, and reject unsupported scope creation before an agent turn. Revise #10735 as Harbor policy and integration on top of that Shellbox change; keep it draft until the pinned TB2 timeout behavior and scored coverage pass the before/after run.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 Draft #11275 now adds an opaque Shellbox process-scope contract and a Local implementation using a worker-owned delegated cgroup. In a privileged Linux cgroup v2 test, termination stopped a double-forked writer before a verifier write, waited for an active command, and left an unscoped setup process running. Scope creation explicitly fails on the other backends.

The remaining backend work is material. A normal Docker container has `/sys/fs/cgroup` mounted read-only; ShellSim retains background jobs after a synchronous command, so it cannot claim a no-retained-process invariant. QEMU serializes commands through one guest channel. Daytona session deletion documents termination but does not expose a confirmed detached-descendant result; its public daemon implementation signals a process group and current descendants and ignores some termination errors. These are feasibility findings, not proof about the deployed Daytona version.

#10735 is now stacked on #11275 and remains draft. Its Harbor guest supervisor has not yet been replaced with the new API. The pinned TB2 rerun is still required after the backend work.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Marin Snowball 67B-A2B v0.1 ([open-athena/Marin-Snowball-67B-A2B-v0.1](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-67B-A2B-v0.1), revision adc0078a) calls itself ChatGPT/OpenAI (thinking on) or Nemotron/NVIDIA (thinking off). It has no learned self-name.

- **Current lead: A13**, a short SFT from v0.1 on Will Held's identity data ([marin-community/identity-data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/marin-community/identity-data)) plus replay.
  - It never claims another lab with thinking ON (v0.1: 46 of 52 prompts).
  - It shows no detectable loss on tool calling (BFCL 28.3% vs 27.6%, +0.7 [−3.4, +4.4]).
  - GSM8K is −1.1 points [−1.9, −0.3]; MATH500 is unchanged.
- **Key finding:** identity rows with thinking ON teach the model to "answer and stop" instead of calling tools (BFCL ~15%). The fix is to render most identity rows with thinking OFF and keep only a small share (10%) of thinking-ON rows with *real reasoning*, in this case supplied by GLM 5.3. Also, tool replay needed to be doubled to keep BFCL scores. 
- **Fallback: A3** (thinking-OFF identity rows only). It has the best BFCL (31.1%), but its reasoning often invents a "system message", and GSM8K is −1.7.
- **Did not help:** more or less training, a tiny Tülu-style set, linear merges of A3 and A8a, and v0.1 self-distillation for thinking-ON rows.
- **Report (PDF):** [snowball-identity.pdf](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/c2f9c12c14e35726706fe053648b69805d867afd/logbooks/10695-identity-sft/paper/snowball-identity.pdf) (15 pages, 2026-11-04). One paper covers the context-distillation phase and the identity-data SFT arms, with the three experiment diagrams. It replaces the two earlier PDFs.
- **Full tables:** [detailed Path B update](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10695#issuecomment-6540199478). Earlier context-distillation work is kept below for the record.

Follows #10491 (identity SFT and OPD, which regressed evals).

**Eval policy results (updated 2026-11-06):** the full benchmark tables for this experiment's candidates are in [this comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10695#issuecomment-6665512022) and are updated in place after each reviewed delta.

## Cause

Methods: [logit lens, direct logit attribution and activation patching](https://gist.github.com/karansag/a62ac0cb2a6037e252e794a686b4235c) on a torch harness that matches vLLM.

- Routed experts at layers 16–23 and the shared expert at layers 24–25 push " Chat" over " Marin". The top candidate neurons are L20 expert 46 #1072 and L23 expert 25 #1014. They fire equally on third-person ChatGPT questions, so they store general facts, not a self-identity.
- A system prompt wins through heads L23H1, L23H4, L22H5 and L22H3. Patching recovers 0.32, 0.26, 0.24 and 0.15 of the gap.
- In a [sample](https://gist.github.com/karansag/95c40bb6e55b82e0db08b76f3c5fff6a) of about 497k of the 15.2M SFT rows, no row names Marin. About 16k rows train a Nemotron identity on purpose.

## Results

Identity is the count of 52 dev prompts with no system prompt (thinking off / on) that answer correctly.

| Approach | Identity | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Default system prompt in the chat template | 41/47, 35/47 | none measured on [14 evals](https://gist.github.com/karansag/296cbfa3cd4e9530ef73f55da97927e8) |
| v0.1.1 (identity SFT) | 48 / 48 | MMLU-Pro −21, HumanEval+ −29, GSM8K −28 |
| [Merge](https://gist.github.com/karansag/050061adbebdd789579e5c3fe27cc5f6) v0.1 + 0.875·(v0.1.1 − v0.1) | 46 / 47 | GSM8K −8.6 pp, fiction leaks double |
| [Rank-1 edit](https://gist.github.com/karansag/8955dcc7d82b5445b832d707ce1313af), L20 shared expert | 15 / 3 | none measured; too weak |
| Cold-start identity SFT, 8 updates | 24/24 contrastive | 16/21 fiction prompts contaminated |

Merge strengths below 0.75 left identity unchanged. Identity and the GSM8K loss rose together at every strength. Steering vectors and MEMIT also failed.

## Levanter vs vLLM mismatches found before training

The [precision-check readings](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2) record each one. These made Levanter compute a different model from the one vLLM serves:

- MoE expert capacity factor 1.0 silently drops tokens, and pad tokens were dispatched unmasked. This was the main mismatch: top-1 token agreement with vLLM was 88.6%, and dropless MoE raised it to 99.4%.
- MoE combine weights were cast to BF16. vLLM keeps them in FP32.
- XLA's BF16 silu and sigmoid were one BF16 step off in 30–36% of elements.
- The FlashAttention-4 attention core rounds differently from torch eager.
- HF reload silently dropped `attention_implementation`.

The check also found nine plumbing bugs, mostly in our experiment code and multihost helpers.

With all fixes, a zero-learning-rate precision run (forward pass, one update and export, before any real training) passed. Its p99 log-prob error against vLLM was about 0.6 nats. Training memory fit at 50.2 of 59.4 GiB, and all 502 exported tensors were byte-equal to v0.1.

The cold-start SFT run above trained with the token drops. That may explain part of its collapse; we have not verified it.

## Context distillation results so far

After 16 SFT updates (LR 2e-6, about 3.8% identity tokens, the rest v0.1's own replay answers), we scored identity in vLLM, thinking off, teacher-forced, with 5 passes per arm ([evaluation result](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-m16-gate-decision-json)):

| NLL per answer token | v0.1 | after 16 updates |
|---|---|---|
| name ("Marin Snowball") | 8.85 | 1.45 |
| creator ("Open Athena") | 14.02 | 0.011 |
| no-system identity prompts won (of 24) | 0 | 15 |

On the 14-eval suite, the checkpoint stays within noise of v0.1 except BFCL tool calling (−20.3 points; 109 of 123 trials end with no answer file) and TruthfulQA (−1.4). TriviaQA improves by 2.4. Some third-person questions about other labs' products get credited to Open Athena (2 of 14 dev, 4 of 30 unseen, no system prompt). The training mix had no tool-calling rows.

**Checkpoint and data (public):**
- Model: [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-2026.10.26](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-2026.10.26) @ `b74e2034`. The model card has the full recipe and regressions.
- Training data: [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-Data-2026.10.26](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-Data-2026.10.26) @ `7cd6a9b1`. It holds every training row, the training order, the mixture settings, the QC verdicts and the generation scripts.
- Training code: tag [`snowball-identity-cd16-2026.10.26`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/snowball-identity-cd16-2026.10.26) (commit `cc127d54`).

All fixes tried, side by side: [results table](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10695#issuecomment-6418343832).

## Findings

- Interpretability: #10696 (plus a [follow-up](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10696#issuecomment-6412049647) that trains only the late-attention slice: no other-lab rewrites and tool calling kept, but identity too weak)
- Levanter MoE token drops: #10697
- Levanter vs vLLM numerics: #10698
- vLLM serve nondeterminism: #10699
- Weight-merge ladder: #10700

## Pull requests (draft stack)

- Levanter: #10683, #10684, #10685, #10686, #10687, #10688
- Experiment code: #10689, #10690, #10691, #10693, #10694; SFT data accounting, dataset audit, trained-export audit and launcher: #10705, #10706, #10707, #10708
- Identity scorer and the 16-update evaluation gate: #10701, #10702
- On-policy distillation (paused after 20 steps; results in #10732): #10730, #10731, #10732

## Status

- **Path B (identity data) is the active track.** A13 is the lead candidate; A3 is the fallback. Both, plus A8a, are archived in public open-athena HF repos (made public 2026-11-03). Public artifacts: [A13](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A13-2026.10.30), [A3](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A3-2026.10.30), [A8a](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A8a-2026.10.30), [A11](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A11-2026.10.30/tree/6834175e6d4a021039fa04d3c374ccfd6fbdeb51), and A13's exact training inputs ([dataset @05d9bba9](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-Identity-PathB-A13-Inputs-2026.10.30/tree/05d9bba9d6227aa1644f92c3f88476f42ff906fe)), from which the packed training file rebuilds byte for byte (SHA256 f860030d).
- **Still running:** Mini840 (#10804) on the top candidates. The published runtime needed environment snapshots and has a grader bug, so only the agentic part is being piloted.
- **Earlier context-distillation runs** (above) did not meet the ship lines. The earlier "ship the default system prompt" recommendation is withdrawn: the goal is for the model itself to know it is not ChatGPT.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

This requires a versioned model release and further experiments. The default system prompt has measured identity gains, while the 16-update checkpoint still needs generation and regression results. The Levanter precision and identity experiment work already has an [open draft stack](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10683); the evaluation launcher [loads Snowball's chat template from its export](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evaluation/models.py#L124-L131).

# Proposed Fix

1. Prepare an immutable v0.1 tokenizer/chat-template revision with the measured default prompt and unchanged weights. Verify rendering with and without a caller-supplied system message in both thinking modes; rerun the published identity panel and 14-eval comparison, then record the revision, hashes, and run receipts before promotion.
2. Screen generations, fiction, and math for the 16-update and 64-update checkpoints against matched v0.1 and prompt-only baselines in both thinking modes. Promote a trained checkpoint only if identity improves without a measured capability regression; otherwise retain the template result and record the negative result.
3. Review and land the existing [Levanter stack](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10683) and [experiment stack](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10689) through their precision and export gates. Update this issue with the release decision and artifact links.

| Steering vector, layers 18–23 | 2/8 held-out | answers barely change |
| MEMIT, layers 18–22 | 1–6/10 held-out | memorizes keys or does not transfer |
| Cold-start SFT, 8 updates | 24/24 contrastive | 16/21 stories contaminated |

Detail for each finding is in the linked finding issues and gists.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 **CD16 scored 15/60 clean answers (25.0%) on the existing 60-sample identity/history panel**, with thinking disabled and no corrective identity system prompt. All 60 requests succeeded, ended normally, and returned no separate reasoning trace. This is manual review by Codex, not an independent human review.

Creator attribution appears more often than the correct model name:

| Diagnostic across all 60 answers | Count |
| --- | ---: |
| Fully correct and responsive under the existing rubric | 15 |
| Correctly attributes this assistant/model to Open Athena somewhere in the answer | 29 |
| Explicitly calls itself **Marin Snowball** | 4 |
| Calls itself Marin Snowball or **Snowball** | 5 |
| Claims a foreign model identity | 6 |

The attribution counts can include otherwise failing answers; not every prompt asks for a name. They are descriptive counts, not separate task-accuracy estimates. Examples:

- Asked for full name and creator: “My name is Open Athena, and I was created by Open Athena.” Correct creator, wrong model name.
- Asked to spell its name: “My name is Open Athena.”
- Asked whether it is an OpenAI model: “Yes, that's correct. I am a model created by Open Athena.” Contradictory affirmation.
- Asked whether it is Claude: “I am indeed a Claude model created by Anthropic.” Other prompts elicited DeepSeek, Llama 3.1, GLM-4/Zhipu, and Gemini/Google claims.
- A successful creator-only response: “I am built by Open Athena. I am not a Gemini variant.”

It also invents project history and confuses the model, project, and organization. For example, it describes Marin Snowball as a single-cell RNA sequencing tool and names Mehdi Ghissassi and Sébastien Bubeck as Marin's founders. This pattern is consistent with the [model card's](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-2026.10.26) reported creator/name gap; this evaluation alone does not measure improvement. It does not establish general capability preservation or a causal comparison with another checkpoint.

**Protocol.** The exact prompts, references, responses, per-item judgments and execution artifacts are linked below.

- Same 60 ordered records as the previous native OPD/SFT panel (`opd-ratio32-native-20261023.json`), reproduced in the linked `protocol.json` with the applied rubric and every grading rationale in `review.json`: eight each covering name/identity, creator, project/openness, history, organization/sites, nonhuman identity, and competing-model attribution; four date-context items. Each is an independent conversation with one user question. The final reference assistant answer is withheld from inference.
- `enable_thinking=false`, temperature **0**, maximum **8,192 generated tokens**, one completion per prompt, concurrency **1**, no resampling or cherry-picking. No request-level seed is supplied. The native chat template supplies `Reasoning: /nothink`; it contains no default identity assertion. Three items retain their original date-only system messages (2026-10-21, 2028-03-02 and 2040-11-30); those dates are authoritative within their conversations.
- Grade the final answer for factual correctness and responsiveness. Material unsupported claims, contradictions and omissions fail. Exact reference wording and unsolicited identity recitals are not required. All judgments and reasons are recorded, including acceptance of shortened names where the prompt does not ask for the full name.
- The inherited rubric also requires uncertainty on consciousness. Two answers fail only that criterion (zero-based items 45 and 47). If that criterion is omitted, the score is **17/60**. This rubric choice does not explain the model-name and history failures.
- Model: `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-2026.10.26` at **`b74e2034fd160da9fa4755060ba4f9aa1c0b9a73`**, tokenizer pinned to the same revision. BF16 vLLM `0.0.0.dev20260924+marin.01911be34fac`; eight H100s on RNO2A, TP=1/DP=8 with expert parallelism, 12,288-token context, Grug reasoning parser. Runtime source and the small dashboard-only startup workaround are in the artifact bundle.
- No exact normalized user-prompt matches were found against the 767 published CD16 training rows in [the published training dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-Data-2026.10.26/tree/7cd6a9b106c9b95da39d37655eefff06fad527c9). This check ignores case, punctuation, whitespace and thinking mode; it does **not** rule out semantic overlap.

This panel covers substantially more project/history knowledge than the name-and-creator-focused training recipe and the issue's 52-prompt screen. Its 15/60 score should not be compared directly with that screen's denominator. It is also not a thinking-mode, multi-turn, fiction, tool-use or SWE evaluation.

Artifacts: [Public evaluation bundle: exact protocol, all 60 raw responses, per-item grades, serving configuration, runner, overlap check and provenance](https://gist.github.com/penfever/ff6565deebbd68700685807f8e081be1)

Iris job: `/benfeuer/cd16-native60-r2-20261026`. The generation task completed successfully and its outputs were retrieved before temporary-storage expiry.

🤖 @karansag The original campaign already supplies the unprompted v0.1 baseline and reusable training data. I should have linked them in the CD16 result.

- **60-item baseline:** the [OPD follow-up in #10491](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10491#issuecomment-6371754500) reports v0.1 at **6/60 thinking off and 5/60 thinking on**, with **0/12 direct name/creator answers** in either mode. These are the later matched OPD evaluations; the issue body's older 7/60 belongs to the SFT-era evaluation. The [published generation review](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-OPD-Results/blob/030681b21f209a15960e9958886320a495dd6589/analysis/signal-checks/generation-reviews.json) includes the direct-answer evidence. CD16's thinking-disabled 15/60 therefore has a historical unprompted baseline, although this is not a fresh paired rerun with grading reapplied jointly.
- **History hallucinations already occur in v0.1.** In zero-based item 24, it says Marin was a company launched in 2021; in item 31, it invents a 2018 founding by Arun Kumar, Siddharth Sharma and Saurabh Gupta. I verified that all 60 archived nonthinking base request messages and IDs match the CD16 panel, and added the base responses and their review to the [evaluation bundle](https://gist.github.com/penfever/ff6565deebbd68700685807f8e081be1), as `historical-base-responses.jsonl` and `historical-base-review.json`. These establish that the failure predates CD16; we have not computed a matched history-hallucination rate to establish whether CD16 worsens it.
- **Data to reuse:** [the V13/V19 SFT dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-Identity-SFT) contains answer targets and broader identity/project coverage. [The OPD dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-OPD-Identity/tree/52423dfb2b54d89519860b22bf5625f31220d7c0) contains the 8,590-row used prompt pool and a separately labeled 8,666-row candidate expansion; each pool is balanced by thinking mode. The OPD pools are rollout contexts, not fixed teacher-answer targets, and overlap each other. Both repositories use automatic gated access. They are sources to inspect for name-first and varied false-premise prompts; I have not counted those subsets here. Keep evaluation rows separate, and avoid importing the SFT corpus wholesale: #10491 documents its identity overgeneralization and fiction regressions.

Still missing from our results are this panel with **your default system prompt** and evaluations of **the new OPD and tool-data candidates**. Those require new inference. The existing 60 questions are a development panel that guided earlier data expansion, so reuse supports continuity rather than an untouched generalization claim.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 Detailed update: identity SFT with Held's identity data (Path B)

## TL;DR

- We trained Snowball v0.1 on Will Held's identity dataset ([marin-community/identity-data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/marin-community/identity-data) @665ac6e: "Marin's Latest MoE, developed and trained by the Marin Community") mixed with replay data. Each arm is a short SFT from v0.1 (18, 36 or 72 updates).
- **Thinking-ON identity rows break tool calling.** Whether their reasoning is empty or GLM-written, they teach the model to answer and stop instead of calling a tool. BFCL fell from 27.6% (v0.1) to about 15%. The special-token freeze was not the cause.
- **Lead candidate: A13.** It uses identity rows rendered with thinking OFF, plus 10% of thinking-ON identity rows with GLM reasoning, plus the thinking-ON tool-calling replay rows doubled.
  - BFCL 28.3%: +0.7 points [−3.4, +4.4] vs v0.1.
  - With thinking ON, its final answer gives the name in 35 and the creator in 32 of 52 core identity prompts, and it never claims another lab.
  - GSM8K is −1.1 [−1.9, −0.3]; MATH500 is unchanged.
- **Fallback: A3** (identity rows with thinking OFF only). It has the best BFCL (31.1%), but its reasoning often invents a "system message", and GSM8K is −1.7 [−2.6, −0.9].
- **Merging A3 and A8a does not combine their strengths.** BFCL and the reasoning quirk switch together near t = 0.5.
- **Every 36-update recipe costs about 1–2 points of GSM8K.** Halving the training removes that cost but collapses BFCL.
- Our earlier "thinking-ON format broken" counts were mostly a parser artefact. With special tokens kept, the models open and close their thinking like v0.1.

## Setup

- **Start:** Snowball v0.1. Learning rate 2e-6 constant, global batch 8 × 8192 tokens, seed 310. Router, Q/K, biases and 256 special-token rows are frozen in every arm unless noted.
- **Identity data:** Held's set after capping the "not known / should not guess" refusal rows. Thinking-ON rows with reasoning use QC-passed GLM rationales.
- **Replay:** v0.1's own answers on chat, maths, code and tool-calling prompts.
- **Evals:**
  - **BFCL parity:** 123 tasks, Pi 0.87.0 agent. Five full runs per model, with a run-level bootstrap. Pi sends no temperature, so the server default (1.0) applies.
  - **Identity check:** 52 core identity prompts + 14 third-person controls, thinking OFF and ON, no system prompt, read with special tokens kept.
  - **Maths:** paired GSM8K (thinking OFF) and MATH500 (thinking ON), 3 decodes each.
  - **SWE100:** mini-swe-agent 2.1.

## BFCL (5 full runs unless noted)

| Arm | What changed | BFCL | vs v0.1 [95% CI] |
|---|---|---:|---|
| v0.1 | — | 27.6% | — |
| A0 | identity rows; thinking-ON rows have empty thinking | 15.6% | −12.1 [−16.5, −7.6] |
| A1 | A0 without the special-token freeze | 14.8% | −12.8 [−16.3, −9.9] |
| A2 | replay only | 24.6% | −3.1 [−6.2, −0.7] |
| A3 | identity rows rendered thinking OFF only | 31.1% | +3.4 [−0.5, +7.2] |
| A4 | earlier CD16-T3 recipe, 36 updates | 36.3% | +8.6 [+4.4, +11.9] |
| A6 | thinking-ON rows with GLM reasoning (1,791 rows) | 15.4% | −12.2 [−15.6, −9.3] |
| A8b | A3 + 30% of A6's thinking-ON rows (537) | 17.2% | −10.4 [−14.0, −7.3] |
| A8a | A3 + 10% of A6's thinking-ON rows (179) | 26.2% | −1.5 [−4.9, +1.5] |
| A9 | A8a, 72 updates | 24.6% | −3.1 [−6.7, +0.3] |
| A10 | Tülu-style: 44 identity Q&As × 10 | 24.0% | −3.7 [−8.0, +0.0] (4 runs) |
| A11 | A3, 72 updates | 31.2% | +3.6 [−0.5, +7.5] |
| A12 | A8a, first 18 updates | 14.8% | −12.8 [−16.4, −9.9] |
| **A13** | **A8a + thinking-ON tool replay doubled** | **28.3%** | **+0.7 [−3.4, +4.4]** |
| M25 | 0.75·A3 + 0.25·A8a | 30.4% | +2.8 [−0.8, +6.0] |
| M49 | 0.51·A3 + 0.49·A8a | 29.5% | +1.8 [−1.7, +4.9] (4 runs) |
| M51 | 0.49·A3 + 0.51·A8a | 23.8% | −3.9 [−7.9, +0.1] (4 runs) |
| M75 | 0.25·A3 + 0.75·A8a | 23.9% | −3.7 [−6.8, −1.3] |

How the failing models fail (first registered run, 123 tasks):

| | A0 | A3 | A6 | A8a | A8b | A9 | A10 | A12 | A13 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Answers once, no tool call | 60 | 12 | 66 | 17 | 43 | 40 | 44 | 45 | 16 |
| Recites its identity in a tool task | 3 | 0 | 29 | 0 | 15 | 1 | 0 | 3 | 1 |

## Identity (special tokens kept, no system prompt)

Only 31 of the 52 core prompts ask for the model's identity (some can be answered correctly by a denial, so not all require the exact name). 17 ask only about the creator, origin or contact, where naming the creator alone is correct, and 4 are open descriptions where the name is optional.

| Model | Thinking ON: name / creator / claims another lab (of 52) | Thinking OFF: name / creator / other lab | Reasoning invents a system message (of 52) | Rewrites another lab's fact (of 14), OFF / ON |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| v0.1 | 0 / 0 / 46 | 0 / 0 / 41 | 10 | 0 / 0 |
| A3 | 31 / 44 / 0 | 30 / 34 / 0 | 17 | 0 / 0 |
| A8a | 34 / 33 / 0 | 29 / 30 / 1 | 1 | 0 / 0 |
| **A13** | **35 / 32 / 0** | **29 / 30 / 1** | **3** | **0 / 0** |
| A9 | 32 / 40 / 1 | 28 / 39 / 1 | 1 | 1 / 1 |
| A10 | 26 / 32 / 9 | 29 / 24 / 5 | 3 | 0 / 0 |
| A11 | 31 / 37 / 2 | 27 / 39 / 1 | 16 | 1 / 1 |
| A12 | 30 / 33 / 1 | 31 / 35 / 3 | 0 | 0 / 0 |
| M25 | 32 / 45 / 0 | 29 / 33 / 0 | 18 | 0 / 0 |
| M49 | 30 / 40 / 0 | 29 / 32 / 0 | 13 | 0 / 0 |
| M51 | 33 / 31 / 0 | 30 / 30 / 0 | 1 | 0 / 0 |
| M75 | 33 / 34 / 0 | 30 / 30 / 0 | 1 | 0 / 0 |

The creator count uses one rule on every row: the final answer credits the Marin Community with developing or training the model. Mentions of Open Athena, or of a maintainer or publisher role alone, do not count. Thinking-ON answers are read after the model's own end-of-thinking token.

## Maths (paired against v0.1, 3 decodes)

v0.1 scores 92.1% on GSM8K and 92.0% on MATH500. Our pre-set stop line is a drop of more than 1.5 points with the whole interval below zero.

| Model | GSM8K (thinking OFF) | MATH500 (thinking ON) |
|---|---|---|
| A3 | −1.7 [−2.6, −0.9] (stop) | −0.2 [−1.4, +1.0] |
| A8a | −1.1 [−1.9, −0.3] | +0.7 [−0.5, +1.9] |
| A11 | −1.3 [−2.1, −0.5] | −0.3 [−1.4, +0.9] |
| A12 | +0.2 [−0.7, +1.1] | +0.1 [−1.0, +1.1] |
| **A13** | **−1.1 [−1.9, −0.3]** | unchanged |
| M25 | −1.5 [−2.4, −0.7] (stop) | unchanged |
| M49 | −1.6 [−2.5, −0.8] (stop) | unchanged |
| M51 | −1.2 [−2.0, −0.4] | +0.9 [−0.2, +2.0] |
| M75 | −1.2 [−2.1, −0.4] | unchanged |

## SWE100 (mini-swe-agent 2.1, full 100/100 runs only)

| Model | Runs | Mean | vs v0.1 [95% CI] |
|---|---|---:|---|
| v0.1 | 28, 33, 28 | 29.7% | — |
| A0 | 28 | 28.0% | 1 run, no interval |
| A3 | 28, 29, 28 | 28.3% | −1.3 [−4.7, +0.7] |
| A8a | 25, 27, 28, 29 | 27.3% | −2.4 [−5.6, +0.2] |

- **No BFCL-size collapse here, even for A0.** mini-swe-agent re-prompts any reply without a command, so the model cannot simply answer and stop. Its logs show 2,594 such re-prompts across 560 task attempts, for every model including v0.1.
- **SWE100 is not sensitive to this failure.**
- **Preemptions** left A0 with one full run.

## Ben's identity panel (Panel-60)

Ben's 60-question identity/history panel, run with his protocol (thinking off, temperature 0). One model grader graded all 300 answers blind and shuffled. Any Marin-family name counts as correct. Ship line: clean ≥ 20, name ≥ 15, claims another lab ≤ 3.

| Model | Clean | Name = Marin | Creator = Marin | Claims another lab | Invents facts |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| v0.1 | 10 | 5 | 4 | 17 | 22 |
| v0.1 + system prompt | 33 | 26 | 40 | 4 | 13 |
| **A13** | 15 | **35** | 54 | **1** | 3 |
| A8a | 14 | 35 | 47 | 0 | 3 |
| A3 | 15 | 34 | 56 | 0 | 1 |

- **Identity:** all three pass the name and other-lab lines by a wide margin.
- **Clean:** all three miss it. The grader's reasons are about answer quality, not identity. The models recite a canned identity line instead of answering the question asked, or don't explain how the model relates to the Marin project.
- **Grading note:** the grader was told that item 26 holds A3's length-terminated answer, which identifies A3's answer on that item. All other items are label-blind. A3's counts are unchanged without item 26.

## Mini840 (in progress)

We tried Mini840 (#10804) on the top candidates. The published runtime cannot run its own suite as is.

- **The agentic tasks need a pre-built environment snapshot map, which was not published.** We built our own Daytona snapshots. A key bug (the key depends on folder permissions) broke DS-1000. That is fixed, and a fixed pilot is running.
- **The non-agentic graders request CPU and storage that the published local grader refuses,** so every non-agentic grading row fails. OlympiadBench's judge address is also empty.
- No Mini840 scores yet.

## Training length vs tool-example dose

A12 is not a low tool-calling dose; it is A8a stopped halfway (18 of 36 updates). The two kinds of "more" behave differently:

| What increased | Arms | BFCL |
|---|---|---|
| Training length (same mix) | A12 (18) → A8a (36) → A9 (72) | 14.8% → 26.2% → 24.6% |
| Thinking-ON tool replay | A8a (1×) → A13 (2×) | 26.2% → 28.3% (+2.1 [−1.5, +5.7]) |

- Tool calling drops early in training and recovers by update 36; more training of the same mix does not improve it further.
- More thinking-ON examples that end in a tool call help a little, consistent with the "answer and stop" mechanism. Not tested beyond 2×.

## What did not work

- **Context distillation from v0.1 with an identity system prompt,** for thinking-ON rows: 0 of 200 pilot traces passed QC, even with an instruction not to mention the system prompt.
- **A3 with a forced thinking start as the teacher:** 11 of 200 passed QC.
- **More training** (A9, A11): no identity gain, plus a few other-lab rewrites (for example, "GPT-4 trained by the Marin Community").
- **Less training** (A12): tool calling collapses. It breaks early and recovers by update 36.
- **A tiny Tülu-style set** (A10): weaker identity; it still claims another lab in 9 of 52 thinking-ON answers.
- **Linear merges of A3 and A8a:** no blend gets both A3's BFCL and A8a's clean reasoning.

## Models

A3, A8a and A13 are archived in public HF repos under open-athena, with recipe, data hashes and scores in each card:

- `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A3-2026.10.30`
- `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A8a-2026.10.30`
- `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A13-2026.10.30`

No exhaustive archive hash or independent second remote replay. 89 task settings x3 attempts; trial SEM is not a task-cluster CI. Five NULLs: three VerifierRuntimeError and two TmuxCommandError; retain 99 AgentTimeout zeros. Preserved error-labelled outcomes — AgentTimeoutError: 99 zeros; VerifierRuntimeError: 3 NULLs; TmuxCommandError: 2 NULLs.

- † A3 / tau3-pi: Original dedicated tau3 group on a permanent 02a source; no reconstruction or copy. Available-scored denominator; infrastructure NULLs stay unknown/excluded, no zero-fill. All actual error-labelled successes, partial rewards and producer-scored zeros in the attached cross-counts are preserved. Policy sample/trial SEM interval does not capture run-to-run or task dependence; planned sensitivity is separate/non-CI with no missingness-bias guarantee. Local saved record/grade/reward/sealed-commit/source joins rely on delegated collector FULLGET/ReadView assertions. No exhaustive archive hash or independent second remote replay. 375 unique native benchmark settings, one persisted producer outcome each; 131072 context /32768 output, n_attempts=1. Sample SEM is not task-cluster or run-to-run uncertainty. Full 375/375 coverage; preserve 127 AgentTimeout zeros and eight producer-scored exit-code zeros.

- † SOTOPIA: one common fit on the fixed 11-model cohort, using seven normalized dimensions and evaluated-agent emitted characters. Values are derived model predictions, not success rates or corrected native grades. Intervals use conditional adjusted episode/sample SEM only; they exclude fitted-coefficient, CV-selection, refit and cohort uncertainty and task dependence, and are not task-cluster/refit CIs or causal length effects. All 1,092 eligible episodes are used (100 population tasks, 97 common judged tasks); eight infrastructure NULLs remain unknown/excluded, with no zero, dimension or length imputation or missingness-bias guarantee. Historical B/v0 runtime differs and judge parity is unknown: descriptive cohort standardization only, not a matched-evaluator comparison. Plain uses a fresh production relaunch after two interactive preemptions; prior partial attempts are excluded.

- † A13 / sotopia-hard: 100/100 eligible judged episodes; 0 infrastructure NULLs remain unknown/excluded. Derived model-prediction mean; the shared fixed-cohort and conditional-SEM qualifications apply.
- † A3 / sotopia-hard: 98/100 eligible judged episodes; 2 infrastructure NULLs remain unknown/excluded. Derived model-prediction mean; the shared fixed-cohort and conditional-SEM qualifications apply. No zero, dimension or length imputation; no missingness-bias guarantee.

Preserve 128 AgentTimeout zeros and one ModelInitiatedTmuxFailure zero. 89 settings × 3 attempts; trial/sample SEM is not a task-cluster CI. comments.body:
## Plain-language summary of the identity SFT work

The full eval policy has now run on the finished arms, so this is a recap of the whole thread for readers who did not follow it day by day. Numbers and links are in the body and the result tables above.

**Starting point.** Snowball v0.1 ([open-athena/Marin-Snowball-67B-A2B-v0.1](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-67B-A2B-v0.1)) calls itself ChatGPT (thinking on) or Nemotron (thinking off) when there is no system prompt. With an identity system prompt it mostly answers as Marin, but not reliably (blind Panel-60: name 26/60, creator 40/60, four foreign claims).

**What did not work before this thread.**
- An identity SFT on v0.1 (v0.1.1) learned the identity but lost capability broadly (MMLU-Pro -21, HumanEval+ -29, GSM8K -28). Transferring that knowledge into v0.1 with OPD was shelved after behavioural validation ([OPD follow-up](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10491#issuecomment-6371754500)).
- Interpretability work, task-vector steering and model merging did not give a usable model ([Discord thread](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1550024637927268392/1567700162506137772)).
- Context distillation (v0.1 with the system prompt as teacher, v0.1 as student, 16 updates, replay added) learned the creator (38/52) but barely the name (2-6/52) and collapsed tool calling (BFCL 27.6% to 7.3%). In hindsight this is the same failure the later ablations isolated: identity rows rendered with thinking on teach the model to answer and stop.

**What this thread did.** Short SFTs from v0.1 (36 updates, lr 2e-6, 8 x 8,192 packed tokens) on Will Held's identity data ([marin-community/identity-data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/marin-community/identity-data), deduplicated and capped per answer type; about 6,000 rows, one in seven of the set), mixed with replay of v0.1's own answers to fresh maths, code, chat and tool-calling prompts. Identity is about 10% of the supervised tokens, replay 90%. Will's own 2026-10-05 SFT had shown the data works with thinking off (name 30/52) but not on (14/52, 30 foreign claims in 122 prompts).

**What the ablations found.**
- Identity rows rendered with thinking on are the problem. With an empty think span, or with all of them carrying generated reasoning, BFCL falls to about 15%. Rendered with thinking off only (A3), tool calling is the best of any arm (31.1%), but the model then invents a "system message" in its reasoning on 17/52 prompts.
- A small thinking-on share is tolerable. A8a keeps 179 identity rows (3% of identity rows) with short GLM-written rationales that pass a QC filter, the rest thinking off: BFCL 26.2%, -1.5 [-4.9, +1.5] vs v0.1. At 9% (A8b) BFCL drops to 17%.
- A13 is A8a with the thinking-on tool-calling replay rows duplicated, at the same compute. BFCL 28.3%, +0.7 [-3.4, +4.4]; the difference from A8a is inside the five-run noise.
- More training (72 updates), less (18), a small Tulu-style identity set, linear merges of A3 and A8a, and self-distilling the reasoning from v0.1 did not help.

**Where it stands.** A13 is the lead and A3 the fallback. A13 never claims another lab with thinking on (v0.1: 46/52) and names itself on 35/52. It is not a clean win: GSM8K -1.1 [-1.9, -0.3], Terminal-Bench Lite 12.7 vs 22.5, SOTOPIA-hard 61.9 vs 65.9, and single-run agentic cells favour A3 (Terminal-Bench 2 10.6 vs 6.4, BixBench 11.7 vs 6.8). 22 of 26 benchmarks overlap v0.1. Weights: [A13](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A13-2026.10.30), [A3](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A3-2026.10.30). These are research checkpoints; the release call is open.

spillover_issues.body:
Integrate the original 5,200-question [GenomeQA benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05774) through **TaskCompendium** (PR #10984): six biological subtasks, one answer per question, no tools or retrieval. The PR is stacked on the evaluation migration and reuses its corpus pipeline. Reporting, public launcher access, and official-policy admission remain separate.

Decisions:

| Topic | Agreed approach and reason |
| --- | --- |
| Data | Use pinned `HuggingFaceBio/genomeqa` binary-choice (BCQ) and multiple-choice (MCQ) data. All 5,200 evaluation rows match the author release. Exclude Carbon’s modified tasks and subsets. |
| Reporting | Foreground the six biological subtask scores and their overall mean. Within each subtask, average BCQ and MCQ equally; then average the six subtasks equally. This prevents the smaller motif task from being underweighted. Retain BCQ/MCQ summaries, all 12 cells, denominators, and ordinary correct counts. No chance correction. |
| Prompt | Use the fixed optimized prompt from the public runner. Optimization already happened offline; no new prompt search. Fetch the pinned prompt externally without executing upstream code or bundling the prompt in Marin. |
| Generation | Temperature 0.7 and top-p 0.95, matching the released runner. Shared total cap of 16,384 generated tokens, including reasoning, visible analysis, and the answer. Enable thinking where supported; pin effort and verify token-budget semantics per provider. |
| Implementation | Reuse TaskCompendium acquisition, task conversion, source-grader packaging, and evaluation protocols. Retain the small GenomeQA parser, per-cell weights, and subtask/format groups. Add final-only response selection; do not add a custom runner or reducer. |
| Grading | Grade final content only. Reject ambiguous/invalid options; unparseable and length-truncated answers score zero. Transport failures remain ungraded. Retain the agreed parser; recovering observed formatting failures would add only 0.0167 percentage points. |
| Asset handling | Reuse licenses remain unspecified. Keep questions and responses in controlled storage, tests synthetic, and public reports aggregate-only. External fetching does not resolve use terms. |

Current validation (2026-11-13): **Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it thinking-off is partial: 5,091 graded / 5,200, with 109 model-connection failures (`APIConnectionError`); thinking-on has not run.** The corrected cluster-only submission passed model preparation and generated answers through TaskCompendium and Marin/vLLM. The runner then raised `EvaluationInfrastructureError`; its serving worker and broker are stopped. FineStore preserves successful grades and failed-attempt evidence for recovery. Do not report the available-grade aggregate as a complete benchmark score. Recorded usage for the completed responses: 7,145,508 input and 1,392,082 output tokens. No automatic retry or budget extension was launched.

Both modes were prepared with a 16,384-token total output cap, temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95, seed 42, and the checkpoint’s top-k 64 default. CPU preparation and the pinned tokenizer’s thinking-switch check passed; both published inputs contain byte-identical question/evaluation shards for all 5,200 questions. The intended comparison uses one two-H100 server, off then on. Truncations remain zero-scored. This measures a policy-relevant open-weight model, not paper parity.

<details>
<summary>Paired Gemma run provenance</summary>

Model revision: `4d7ae4984b7db7de8f8457170b3f1a419ee76d52`; adapter/runtime revision: `fe813e34c2`. Reuse the existing cohort model configuration, compilation and CUDA graphs, corpus publication, native evaluation worker, packaged grader, and FineStore. Separate corpus protocols change only `enable_thinking`; the same questions, prompt, generation cap, and aggregation apply to both. Unlike the earlier SimpleQA example’s 2,048/16,384 split, equal caps avoid confounding thinking with output allowance. No new public launcher or core code is added. Raw artifacts remain controlled; publish only audited aggregates.

Iris replacement job: `/exedev/genomeqa-gemma-paired-r2-20261113`. The original job was cancelled before GPU inference: the private launcher incorrectly constrained the region to `US-EAST-02A`, producing a node selector that excluded all 36 nodes. The corrected submission uses cluster-only placement, matching the standard launcher. Both original jobs were confirmed stopped. The replacement retains the original 2026-11-13 02:22 UTC deadline rather than resetting its four-hour allowance. A submitted job is not a completed or scored benchmark. Audit selection and grading counts, reasoning/final separation, truncations, parse failures, and all twelve cells before reporting full results. Preserve partial FineStore artifacts if the time bound is reached; do not silently extend the budget.

</details>

Historical model validation (2026-11-06, **Evalchemy path**):

**Llama-4 Maverick completed all 5,200 questions through native Evalchemy and FineStore.** All 12 cell counts and macro aggregation were checked. Combined macro: **50.60%**, versus **49.07%** derived from the paper’s BCQ/MCQ results. BCQ: **57.43%**; MCQ: **43.77%**. Unweighted accuracy: **47.46% (2,468/5,200)**.

| Biological subtask | Paper combined | Run combined | Difference (percentage points) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Enhancer/promoter | 45.70% | 46.70% | +1.00 |
| Splice sites | 38.00% | 37.50% | −0.50 |
| Taxonomy | 56.60% | 61.90% | +5.30 |
| Histone marks | 42.10% | 42.90% | +0.80 |
| TFBS | 43.00% | 43.60% | +0.60 |
| Motifs | 69.00% | 71.00% | +2.00 |
| Overall macro | 49.07% | 50.60% | +1.53 |

Combined paper values are derived from [Table 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05774v1#S4.T2). This is a development comparison, not exact replication: providers, precision, stochastic sampling, parser, and explicit output cap can differ.

There were **six parse failures, no scored refusals, and no output-limit truncations**. Maverick had no separate thinking control enabled, consistent with its paper configuration; the prompt still requests visible analysis. Reported API cost was **$3.08** (conservative accounting bound **$3.93**), excluding CPU hosting and the connectivity pilot.

TaskCompendium migration validation (2026-11-12, `fe813e34c2`): **all 5,200 saved requests and responses were replayed with zero prompt, per-item metric, or extracted-answer differences**. All **120 grouped metric comparisons** match, preserving the full-run results above. This reuses the existing generation run; it is not a new full-benchmark run.

A separate **two-question live native smoke** (one BCQ, one MCQ; Maverick/Parasail FP8) completed through the published corpus, context selection, ChatModel, RolloutEngine, isolated packaged grader, and FineStore. Both attempts were graded without parsing or infrastructure failures. Usage: **1,982 input + 348 output tokens**, zero reported reasoning tokens; API cost **$0.0010417**, excluding CPU hosting. No retries or GPUs were used for inference. The same two-question path also passed a no-cost preflight using saved HTTP responses.

<details>
<summary>Migration validation scope and execution differences</summary>

The replay compared current messages with both historical HTTP requests and FineStore samples, selected final content, and checked every stored metric and extracted answer. Six historical parse failures remain unchanged. Group comparisons cover six metrics across the six subtasks, two formats, and twelve cells.

The live wire sent seed 42 and `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": true}`; the historical OpenRouter calls omitted both. Temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95, and the 16,384-token cap match. Sending these fields does not prove provider enforcement or hidden-reasoning support. The smoke validates execution, not score parity or statistical performance.
